title: Xcel-funded Pano AI camera catches the Wellington fire near Breckenridge; crews hold it to one-eighth of an acre
summary: Xcel-funded Pano AI camera alerted crews to a campsite fire east of a Breckenridge neighborhood; firefighters said the early notice kept it to one-eighth of an acre (CBS Colorado, 9 July 2024).
account: CBS Colorado reported on 9 July 2024 that a wildfire which broke out at an unattended campsite just east of a Breckenridge neighborhood, the Wellington fire, was spotted by a Pano AI camera financially supported by Xcel Energy. The camera sits on a cell tower with a 360-degree view and submits an alert to emergency crews if it notices smoke. Firefighters said this was the first instance in Summit County where a wildfire was caught early and kept to only one-eighth of an acre thanks to the camera's early notice, after earlier false alarms from legal campfires. Mathew Benedict of Red White and Blue Fire's Wildland Division said a location with an actual lat/long let crews drive straight to the fire instead of spending up to an hour finding it. Xcel's Michelle Aguayo said the company had 28 Pano AI cameras installed. The date of the fire itself is not given; the date used is the article's publication date.
purpose: Pano AI cameras scan for smoke and alert emergency crews with a location; catching a fire near homes early was the intended use.
deployer: Xcel Energy (camera funding); alerts received by Red White and Blue Fire
taxonomy_note: Public-safety containment has no Trustible category; the mechanism (a located alert that removed up to an hour of searching) is organizational efficiency. Harm prevented rests on the fire division's statement that the camera's early notice kept the fire to one-eighth of an acre.

ratings.reason: A fire next to a residential neighborhood was kept to one-eighth of an acre; firefighters credit the camera's early notice, though the counterfactual is their judgment.
Red White and Blue Fire received an exact location and drove straight to the fire; Benedict said locating a wildfire can otherwise take an hour.

ai_role.statement: The camera's AI smoke alert was the trigger for dispatch according to the fire division quoted by CBS Colorado; the only source is a single local news report with named sources, and the fire's date, cause of containment and any official report are not documented.
